svg.title: The granite ledge nearest the viewer on the barrens: ONE continuous surface of bare rounded rock, modelled by broad overlapping domes of the three `path` tones and broken only by a few hairline joints that run along where one swell of rock meets the next, with grass and crowberry in the joints, yellow lichen, and two shallow tide pools. THIS TILE TOOK FIVE GOES AND EACH FIXED A DIFFERENT MISREAD, SO ALL FIVE ARE RECORDED. (1) It began as fourteen near-rectangles in straight rows over a dark ground, and the bottom third of this level read as a paved street of flagstones. (2) Irregular blocks gave crazy paving. (3) Larger, fewer blocks gave big paving flags - because the thing doing the work was never the shape of the blocks, it was that the tile was drawn as SEPARATE PIECES SEEN AGAINST A DARK GROUND, and a dark line that closes all the way around a shape is mortar whatever shape it encloses. So the dark ground went and the tile is filled with the rock itself. (4) That read as dark twigs on striped ground: the tonal fields ran the full width as parallel ribbons, which is bedding in sandstone rather than a granite whaleback, and the cracks were bars of constant width floating clear of them. The fields became TEN OVERLAPPING DOMES, five `path-base` and five `limestone-light`, each wider than it is tall with a rounded crown and no straight edge. (5) The cracks still read as thorns lying on the surface, because a tapered sliver that touches nothing is a splinter. There are six joints now rather than ten, each about two px wide instead of six, and four of the six RUN ALONG THE EDGE OF A DOME - the line where one swell of rock meets the next, which is where a joint in bare rock actually shows - so they read as part of the surface rather than as objects on it. Nothing on this tile encloses anything. Kept from earlier: THE TIDE POOLS ARE NOT DISCS. Each was concentric ellipses ringed in `brass-shade`, and a bright warm ring around a flat blue disc set in grey paving is a drain lid - which is what the scene showed, twice. Each pool is an irregular hollow with its long axis across the rock, water in two flat tones, glints as two short straight bars, and rockweed as three or four broken dark tufts gathered on ONE side. That is how `layer-40-granite-barrens` already drew its pools, and this tile now matches the layer it continues. A repeating strip over the ground fill (ADR-0042), world y 1280..1920; local y 0 is the level ground line. GENERIC BY CONSTRUCTION: no erratic, lighthouse or building.
